column4: dialect-gated per SUBTEST: a registeredBackends test, so it runs one subtest per dialect and mysql and mssql skip in these PostgreSQL-only jobs while postgres RUNS -- two, not three. Measured by name rather than by delta, with CLEAT_TEST_MYSQL and CLEAT_TEST_MSSQL unset: the run reports exactly the mysql and mssql arms skipping and the postgres arm passing. The skip is inside StoreBackend.Setup, not in the test -- Setup distinguishes 'nothing configured' (skip) from 'configured and unreachable' (fatal), which a guard in the test would flatten into one skip. The arms have to exist even where they skip: cleat#1460 is about three dialects DISAGREEING on which workflow results they accept -- postgres refuses a NUL escape that mysql and mssql store, mssql accepts a lone surrogate the other two refuse -- so a postgres-only run cannot vouch for the typed detection in the other two arms, which key on entirely different driver error types (MySQL SQLSTATE 22032, SQL Server error 13606).
